correctness.rationale: Deleting one bridge endpoint u and then its closed neighborhood gives the base D=Ind(P_(p-1))*Ind(C_q) and link L=Ind(P_(p-3))*Ind(P_(q-1)), with Y the homotopy cofiber of L→D. When p≡1 the link is contractible; when p≡2 the base is contractible. When p≡0 and p>=6 the inclusion in the first path factor is null because it is a map from a sphere of dimension a-2 to one of dimension a-1; at p=3 the link maps through the equatorial Ind(C_q) in its suspension, which cones off. A join with the null first-factor map is null. Substitution of the path/cycle formulas gives rows (3,2,1), (2,1,1), (1,1,0) with all sphere summands in the claimed dimension. The removed simplices for bridge insertion are precisely those containing {u,v}; the closed star in X meets Y along its edge boundary joined with R=Ind(P_(p-3))*Ind(P_(q-3)). If a residue equals 1 this intersection and the star are both contractible, so the inclusion is an equivalence by a pushout along cofibrations, not merely by inferring equivalence from a contractible quotient. Otherwise the quotient is the double suspension of R, with (3,3) interpreted literally as an interval with its endpoints identified. The long exact sequence gives H_d(Y)→H_d(X) injective with free rank-one cokernel, using reduced homology for d=1; its splitting is integral, not canonical. Inspected `verify.py`, `verification_output.txt` and `VERIFICATION.md`. Their 72 absolute and 36 relative GF(2) results are the recorded bounded checks, not an integral or homotopy proof; the proof also handles the vacuous wedge and empty path.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad graph-class theorems give qualitative or partial constraints but not all nine ranks and degrees or the map on integral homology. The general edge sequence determines the cofiber but not, on its own, the maps from absolute to relative homology.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The further steps are to control the vertex-link inclusion by a nullhomotopy of one join factor (or contractibility in the other residues), evaluate the wedge summands including the triangle cases, and use the support degrees to force the short exact sequence. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A matching complex is the independence complex of a line graph, not that of the starting bridge graph. The vertex identification problem also has different deletion links. The edge-removal formalism does apply and must be credited for the relative cofiber method.

value.rationale: Connecting two cycles is a natural first nontrivial test of how homotopy and integral homology change when a bridge is inserted in a cactus. The full table distinguishes equivalence, loss of one primitive direct summand, and even sphere-to-contractible behavior. This gives information that a qualitative wedge result or knowledge of a relative cofiber alone leaves unresolved; no applicability to longer bridges or arbitrary cactus families is implied.
